evidence: app/src/api.ts:107-160 — every API call, type definition, humanization and URL helper behind one module; API or filter changes touch one file
app/src/api.ts:6 — API_BASE_URL computed in one place
app/package.json:7 — "type": "module" ESM-only, matching hono v5's ESM-only requirement (skill: v5 needs Node 22.12+)
app/src/index.tsx:41-49 — htmx responses distinguished via documented HX-Request header and Vary, no internals
app/src/components.tsx:64 — route path strings duplicated across JSX (also pages/pokemon.tsx:139, pages/details.tsx:47) instead of a central routes helper
app/src/api.ts:172 — spriteUrl hardcodes the /media/sprites/pokemon/<id>.png convention rather than using sprites.front_default where data provides it
churn_resistance.rationale: A single typed data module, one-line config, ESM output and adapter-package imports make a hono v5 upgrade nearly free; route strings and the sprite-URL convention are the only places URL changes would ripple beyond one file.

findings.issue: Upstream fetches have no AbortSignal/timeout; combined with the MAX_CONCURRENT=16 semaphore (api.ts:12-16), 16 hung API calls would block all data loading indefinitely.
findings.suggestion: Pass AbortSignal.timeout(10_000) (or similar) to fetch, and clear the in-flight slot in the existing finally block.

findings.issue: spriteUrl derives sprite URLs from the spec-documented path pattern rather than the sprites.front_default field the API already returns for every fetched Pokémon.
findings.suggestion: Use the API-provided sprite URL where the Pokémon object is already in hand (detail pages, cards built from fetched pokemon data), keeping the pattern only as a fallback for index-only lists.

findings.issue: Route path templates ('/pokemon/…', '/types/…', '/moves/…', '/abilities/…') are duplicated as string literals across components and pages (pokemon.tsx:139, details.tsx:47, home.tsx:79).
findings.suggestion: Centralise link builders in one module (like homeUrl already does) so a future URL scheme change touches one file.

findings.issue: app.js is loaded as a classic script; module scripts are the platform default and give implicit defer + scoping.
findings.suggestion: Add type="module" (and drop defer) to the /static/app.js script tag.

findings.issue: htmx attribute usage relies on the form-element triggers being the request origin; this is correct on 2.x but htmx 4 (released 2026-08-28, not yet npm latest) makes attribute inheritance explicit.
findings.suggestion: When moving to htmx 4, verify the form-issued requests still resolve hx-target/hx-swap (they should, since the attributes sit on the requesting element) — a migration note in the repo would help.

summary: This is a genuinely current codebase: every dependency is pinned at npm latest (hono 4.13.14, node-server 2.1.5, htmx 2.0.11, TypeScript 7 native), imports already use the adapter-package paths hono v5 will require, and all data access sits behind one well-typed module with a sensible hand-rolled SWR cache. The htmx usage is modern and quietly upgrade-proof: hx-* attributes live on the requesting elements, not on children via inheritance. The only real aging risk is the missing AbortSignal on upstream fetches, plus minor duplication of route path strings and the pattern-derived sprite URLs.
